atoms.name: Turing machine steps
atoms.one_line: A transition reads a cell, writes a symbol, moves the head and changes state; trace it step by step.

atoms.name: Equivalent models
atoms.one_line: Multi-tape, non-deterministic and two-way tapes accept the same languages as a single-tape TM.

atoms.name: Recursive versus RE
atoms.one_line: A decider halts on every input; a recogniser may loop on non-members; both RE gives recursive.

atoms.name: Halting and undecidable problems
atoms.one_line: Halting, acceptance, emptiness and equality of TMs are undecidable; the halting language is RE and its complement is not.

atoms.name: Rice's theorem
atoms.one_line: Every non-trivial property of L(M) is undecidable; properties of M's description are not covered.

atoms.name: Reductions
atoms.one_line: A ≤m B passes decidability and RE-ness from B back to A, and undecidability and non-RE-ness from A forward to B.

atoms.name: Countability
atoms.one_line: Machines are countable, languages uncountable, so non-RE languages exist.

atoms.name: Bounded versions
atoms.one_line: A step bound makes a question decidable by simulation, even 'for all inputs', because only a bounded prefix matters.

patterns.name: Closure and relations among RE and recursive
